statement.text:
Elements a, b of a group G are said to be symmetric with respect to an element
g ∈ G if a = gb−1 g. Let G be an infinite abelian group, α a cardinal, α < |G|. Is it
true that for any n-colouring χ : G → {0, 1, . . . , n − 1} there exists a monochrome
subset of cardinality α that is symmetric with respect to some element of G? This is
known to be true for n ⩽ 3.                                               I. V. Protasov
